items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: The fellow Rick Montalbano I mentioned, told me a singer joke

ctx.x: And we were talking about that, you know you broached that earlier, that there is a definite separation. And some musicians don’t like you because you sing the head. Some musicians don’t like you because they don’t think you’re as talented as they are musically because you’re not a musician. So the burden of a singer is to get through those elements that are holding you down. You have to prove to them that you belong there, number one, and the best way to do that, I have found, is with time and to become — at…

That’s right. The fellow Rick Montalbano I mentioned, told me a singer joke, it was real though. You know. Someone wanted to sing a tune with him and he said — I have to get this right — he said, “That’s a little high can you do it in minor?”
